items.content: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The latest edition of our Stepback newsletter should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning. That includes rumors that Jensen Huang might be trying to find a path back to CEO, and a statement from Megaspeed claiming that Alice Huang hasn’t worked for the company since August of 2025, which raises more questions than it answers.Some big names, including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have publicly thrown their support behind a public letter demanding Nvidia “bring Jensen back.”The public letter calling for Jensen Huang to be reinstated has over 150,000 signatures, but it’s difficult to verify their authenticity. Business Insider reports that signatures include “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor” and “Xi Jingping,” likely a misspelling of Chinese president Xi Jinping.The Financial Times reports that Jensen Huang has discussed the possibility of returning as CEO with close allies, as some Silicon Valley insiders and employees attempt to pressure the board.Not all believe Jensen Huang should be allowed to return to his seat. According to the Financial Times, one ally acknowledged that, “Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense.”23andMe founder Anne Wojcicki told Bloomberg that “Power corrupts, and people start to think they are invincible … We are all complicit in making these people think they are gods. And people do stupid things when they think they are untouchable.”Wojcicki endured a messy public divorce from Google co-founder Sergey Brin, after it was revealed he was having an affair with an employee.According to Bloomberg, many women in Silicon Valley see Jensen Huang as simply another example of a rich man abusing their position and “leveraging power to pursue sexual relationships with their employees.”Megaspeed released a statement saying that Alice Huang left the company “effective Aug. 30, 2025, and currently has no role with the company,” adding that “Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters.”

items.titleZh: 黄仁勋或正谋划回归，以及更多英伟达最新闹剧
items.descriptionZh:
这篇英文报道聚焦英伟达（Nvidia）联合创始人、前CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）的复职风波，属于公司治理、高管丑闻与硅谷权力文化新闻，而非AI芯片技术发布。原文未涉及芯片架构、制程、算力、带宽、能效、性能对比或应用场景等技术信息，因此无法从中提取核心技术原理和创新点；以下摘要集中梳理事件背景、各方表态及其可能影响。

事件正在快速演变。Stepback newsletter最新一期原本用于帮助读者了解背景，但自当天上午以来又出现多项新进展：有传闻称黄仁勋可能正试图寻找重返CEO职位的路径；Megaspeed则发表声明称，Alice Huang自2025年8月30日起已离开公司，目前在公司没有任何角色，并称公司不对其个人和私人事务置评。报道认为，这一声明反而引发更多疑问，而非解答问题。

公众层面，一封要求英伟达“让Jensen回来”的公开信已获得超过15万个签名，但签名真实性难以核实。Business Insider报道称，签名者中出现“Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor”和“Xi Jingping”等署名，后者很可能是中国国家主席习近平英文名的拼写错误，显示签名列表存在明显不可信或恶搞成分。尽管如此，埃隆·马斯克和Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney等知名人物已公开支持这封公开信。

据《金融时报》报道，黄仁勋已与亲密盟友讨论过重返CEO职位的可能性，同时一些硅谷内部人士和员工正试图向董事会施压。不过，并非所有人都认为应允许他回归。报道援引一名盟友的话称，“与下属发生婚外情是可被解雇的行为”。23andMe创始人Anne Wojcicki对彭博社表示，“权力会腐蚀人，人们开始觉得自己不可战胜……我们都在让这些人以为自己像神一样。当人们觉得自己不可触碰时，就会做蠢事。”Wojcicki曾与谷歌联合创始人Sergey Brin经历一场公开而混乱的离婚，此前Brin被曝与一名员工有婚外情。彭博社还称，许多硅谷女性将黄仁勋视为富人滥用职位、“利用权力追求与员工发生性关系”的又一例证。

整体来看，该事件的核心争议包括：黄仁勋是否应重返CEO、董事会将如何应对内部员工和外部公众压力、公开信签名真实性与舆论操纵问题，以及高管与下属之间的权力不对等和公司治理风险。对公司层面而言，领导层稳定性、声誉和战略执行可能受到影响；但原文没有提供任何AI芯片技术参数、产品路线图或可量化业务数据，因此无法据此评估技术性能或应用影响。

items.content: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also sent letters to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the committee.Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act, first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are receiving renewed interest. While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters. Johnson has also said that he personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful AI chips from companies like Nvidia.RelatedAn overview of Jensen Huang’s messy daysJensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO

items.titleZh: 美国国会拟在英伟达间谍丑闻后收紧AI芯片出口规定
items.descriptionZh:
报道称，在英伟达前CEO黄仁勋卷入与一名疑似中国间谍有关的丑闻后，美国国会正寻求进一步限制AI芯片出口。文章将黄仁勋称为“现已卸任”的英伟达CEO，并称民主党和共和党都支持收紧规则的多项措施和法案，同时要求黄仁勋及其他英伟达高层赴国会作证。参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默表示，黄仁勋和特朗普政府需要向国会作出交代；参议院银行委员会主席蒂姆·斯科特已分别致信黄仁勋和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克，要求他们公开到该委员会作证。

立法层面，2025年4月首次在众议院提出、后在参议院停滞的《远程访问安全法案》重新受到关注。原文未展开该法案具体条款，但从名称看，其重点涉及远程访问安全，可能与堵塞通过远程方式获取受出口管制技术或算力的漏洞有关。报道同时指出，该具体法案未必最终成为法律，但众议院议长迈克·约翰逊称，国会内部对限制对华芯片出口“正在形成越来越大的共识”，并称他个人支持限制中国获取英伟达等公司的强大AI芯片。

从背景看，AI芯片是训练和运行大模型、建设数据中心和高性能计算集群的关键硬件，美国近年来一直通过出口管制限制中国获得高端GPU和AI加速器。此次报道的核心不是某一款芯片的架构、制程、算力或带宽等性能参数，而是政治与监管风险：一场涉及黄仁勋和疑似中国间谍的丑闻，正在把英伟达及AI芯片出口问题推向国会听证和立法博弈。若国会进一步收紧出口规则，可能影响英伟达对华业务、AI芯片供应链以及中国获取高端算力的渠道；同时，国会要求高管作证也意味着企业面临更强的公开问责和政治压力。文章相关链接还提到“黄仁勋混乱的日子”以及“有远见的表演型创始人CEO的衰落”，显示该报道将个人丑闻、公司治理与AI芯片出口管制政策联系在一起。原文未提供具体技术原理、创新点或对比性能数据。

items.title: Nvidia engineer leaves company over lack of transparency around Jensen Huang’s exit, details decision
items.description: Dai's post shows how much Nvidia employees looked up to the former CEO.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Just days after Jensen Huang suddenly resigned from his position at Nvidia, an Nvidia Robot Research Engineer said that he would leave the company as well. But more than just showing support for the former CEO with a generic “I stand with Jensen” message, Darrel Dai laid out several reasons for the decision on X.I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say. As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO. I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI. I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in. But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build. Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard. That is why this has been so disappointing. I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny. What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me. I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected. I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day. A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too. Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close. I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me. These are my personal views.November 15, 2026“What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me,” the engineer posted. “I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.”It seems that Jensen Huang has gained the respect of the people working under him, with many calling for his reinstatement despite the many controversies he is currently facing. There’s also an online petition demanding that the Nvidia board “Bring Jensen Back,” with over 150,000 signatures at the time of writing.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Nvidia is centered around Jensen Huang, with the former chief executive reportedly having a small army of 60 people directly reporting to him. But despite his busy schedule and legendary persona, Dai said that “Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly,” and that “It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.” Dai also pointed out that “employees’ trust and sense of belonging” are part of what makes a company great. More importantly, Nvidia is known as one of the tech companies with the most generous pay packages. Jensen was even quoted saying, “I pay my employees as much as I can.”It remains unclear what the former Nvidia CEO will do after all these issues. Elon Musk has already said on X that “it would be an honor” to hire Jensen Huang, especially as he’s embarking on his own ambitious chipmaking journey. As for the employees left behind at Nvidia, some are staying and have shown their full support to interim CEO Colette Kress, while many more want him back. However, there has also been talk that various Silicon Valley tech and semiconductor firms are aggressively attempting to poach Nvidians, although these are just rumors so far. items.titleZh: 英伟达工程师因黄仁勋退出缺乏透明度而离职，并详述决定
items.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware报道，在英伟达CEO黄仁勋突然辞职数日后，英伟达机器人研究工程师Darrel Dai宣布也将离开公司，并在X平台发长文说明原因。此事不只是“站队”表态，而是折射出黄仁勋辞职对英伟达内部工程师文化和员工信任的冲击。

Dai表示，他眼中的黄仁勋不只是CEO，更是愿意押注“尚未显而易见的未来”的领导者。黄仁勋在深度学习热潮到来前很久就重注CUDA，使英伟达在AI成为行业优先事项之前完成基础设施布局。CUDA的核心意义在于让GPU能够以并行方式执行通用计算任务，并通过编程模型和软件生态把开发者、AI框架与英伟达硬件连接起来，形成从训练到推理的算力平台。Dai还提到，他在“物理AI”方向看到同样的愿景：投资机器人、共享开源工具和项目、构建把AI带入物理世界的计算平台。物理AI通常指机器人、具身智能等系统在真实环境中完成感知、决策和执行，需要仿真训练、实时推理、边缘计算和软硬件协同平台。原文没有披露具体芯片型号、算力、功耗或基准对比数据，报道重点并非产品性能，而是人事变动与工程文化。

Dai尤其看重黄仁勋塑造的工程文化：鼓励工程师探索、冒险、从错误中学习；即使公司规模庞大，黄仁勋也会阅读员工的“Top 5”邮件、跟踪员工工作并直接互动，让个体工程师感到自己的想法仍能被听见。文章还提到，英伟达以薪酬慷慨著称，黄仁勋曾表示会尽可能高薪支付员工。Dai称，黄仁勋的愿景和工程文化是他愿意留在英伟达的重要原因。

对于黄仁勋辞职所涉指控，Dai表示自己没有掌握全部事实，也不预判调查，并且认为对黄的钦佩不能使其免于审查。但他难以接受的是，在尚未获得能帮助自己理解辞职的解释之前，就要接受黄离开；公司方向、文化以及具体做事的人将受到何种影响仍不清楚。他说自己一直感到工程师视角在英伟达受到重视，但在这项决定上“没有感到被听见”，这种落差比预期更痛苦。他理解部分信息不能立即分享，但这不能消除被排除在影响公司日常建设的决策之外的感觉。公司伟大来自领导力、治理以及把雄心变成现实的人，员工的信任和归属感也是其中一部分。最终，他带着悲伤和感激决定结束自己在英伟达的篇章。

报道显示，黄仁勋在部下中获得了相当尊重，许多人呼吁其复职。网上请愿要求英伟达董事会“Bring Jensen Back”，截至报道时已有超过15万签名。英伟达被认为高度围绕黄仁勋运转，据称有约60人直接向他汇报。部分员工支持临时CEO Colette Kress，但更多人希望黄仁勋回归；同时有传闻称硅谷科技和半导体公司正积极挖角英伟达员工。Elon Musk也在X上表示，雇用黄仁勋“将是一种荣幸”，尤其在他推进自己的芯片制造计划之际。整体来看，这篇报道的核心不是新技术发布，而是英伟达在创始人式CEO突然离职后，如何面对工程师文化、组织信任、人才留存和领导层过渡的不确定性。

items.title: Nvidia RTX 5090 stock returns to Newegg with 21 models
items.description: After rumors of Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards being withdrawn from the consumer retail channel it is pleasing to see major U.S. eTailers like Newegg stuffed with cheaper stock today.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter After rumors of Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards being withdrawn from the consumer retail channel, it is pleasing to see major U.S. e-tailers like Newegg stuffed with stock today. Checking out this popular online electronics retailer, we note that there are 21 RTX 5090 SKUs available, and 11 are sold by and shipped by Newegg. Sadly, pricing remains in 3x MSRP+ territory at the time of writing. Remember, you can sift through pricing trends in our comprehensive GPU price tracking 2026 feature to see that Nvidia's Blackwell flagship was once available at its fabled sub-$2,000 price. (Image credit: Newegg)Despite what looks on the surface like an ample supply (but there are order limits of one per customer), prices for RTX 5090s remain extremely high. The best prices we can see at Newegg are $6,599, but this price applies only to a water-cooled Aorus model and another sold inside a Gigabyte AI BOX eGPU. They might still appeal to you, depending on your setup, though.For a ‘standard’ air-cooled graphics card, albeit a very nice Aorus RTX 5090 Master, you’ll need to squeeze at least $6,659 out of your savings. A bonus with this card, alongside several others from the Gigabyte stables now purchasable from Newegg, is that it comes with a free motherboard. Many of these Gigabyte Aorus designs are being bundled with a full-ATX-sized X870 Aorus Elite WIFI7 AM5 motherboard, purportedly worth $319. Please note that the same motherboard is available to purchase outside this bundle for a more reasonable $249.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: If you have money to burn, there are plenty of even more expensive SKUs to pick from. There are no opulent Golden Dhabab models on Newegg, sadly, but you’ll still be asked to part with $11,896 for the Asus ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 Edition 20 (sold by a Newegg marketplace partner). Perhaps surprisingly, given recent trending pricing news, that’s the only model above $10K, but there are still many models that are almost $10,000 from Asus, MSI, and Zotac. Even an Nvidia Founders Edition RTX 5090 refurb is priced at $8,899.In context, these RTX 5090s are still at astronomical prices for consumer gaming PC add-in hardware. But they are now purchasable from a big retailer with fast delivery, rather than off a random scalper. It was only a month ago that rumors swirled about the RTX 5090 and the RTX 5080 being withdrawn from retail. That seemed to trigger crazy levels of price inflation, and reports of $10,000+ prices for the flagship card seemed to become the norm. items.titleZh: 英伟达 RTX 5090 现货重返新蛋，涵盖 21 款型号
items.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware报道，此前有传闻称Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090和RTX 5080将退出美国零售渠道，并引发旗舰显卡价格剧烈上涨，RTX 5090一度出现1万美元以上报价成为常态。如今，美国大型在线零售商Newegg重新上架了较多RTX 5090库存：共有21个SKU，其中11个由Newegg自营销售并发货，但每个客户限购一张。供应看似改善，价格却仍处于建议零售价（MSRP）3倍以上的区间，远未回归正常。

从价格看，Newegg上RTX 5090最低可见价格为6599美元，但仅适用于水冷版Aorus型号以及装在Gigabyte AI BOX外置GPU坞中的版本；标准风冷型号中，Aorus RTX 5090 Master至少需要6659美元。部分Gigabyte Aorus显卡还捆绑一块全ATX规格的X870 Aorus Elite WIFI7 AM5主板，官方称价值319美元，但该主板单独购买价格为249美元。更昂贵的选项包括由Newegg市场第三方销售的Asus ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 Edition 20，售价11896美元，是页面上唯一超过1万美元的型号；Asus、MSI和Zotac仍有多款接近1万美元的产品，甚至Nvidia Founders Edition RTX 5090翻新卡也标价8899美元。作为对比，Blackwell旗舰RTX 5090曾出现过低于2000美元的价格，而RTX 5080也曾被报道涨至2000美元，超过RTX 5090首发价且库存有限；Nvidia商店还曾撤下RTX 5080和RTX 5090商品页面。

技术层面，RTX 5090是Nvidia Blackwell架构的消费级旗舰显卡，主要面向高端游戏PC、内容创作、AI推理和小型工作站等场景；水冷版、风冷版以及AI BOX外置GPU方案的区别主要在散热形态和系统集成方式，而非本文重点讨论的规格性能。此次新闻的核心并非新硬件发布，而是高端GPU零售渠道的供需失衡：Newegg恢复库存和限购措施有助于抑制部分黄牛与第三方加价，但当前价格仍显著偏离MSRP，捆绑主板和eGPU套装也提高了实际购买门槛。若Newegg及其他渠道的库存持续流入，RTX 5090和RTX 5080价格有望逐步回落；否则，高端游戏与AI工作站用户的升级成本仍将维持高位。

items.title: Intel reclaims overall CPU market share for the first time since 2025
items.description: AMD continues to gain server CPU market share amid skyrocketing shipments of data center processors as sales of client CPUs drop in the third quarter, says Mercury Research.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Shipments of x86 CPUs declined quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year in the third quarter as demand for client processors dropped sharply due to high component prices, while server CPU unit sales grew by a whopping 20% year-over-year, according to the latest report from Mercury Research. Intel regained overall CPU market share from AMD for the first time since Q2 2025, largely due to surprisingly strong performance in desktop PCs. Meanwhile, AMD continued to set new records in the mobile and server CPU segments, the report claims. In total, the industry supplied 68.93 million x86 CPUs, Jon Peddie Research reports. Swipe to scroll horizontally Overall x86 CPU market shares Segment AMD Q3 2026 Intel Q3 2026 AMD QoQ gain AMD Q3 2025 Intel Q3 2025 AMD YoY gain Overall x86 30.10% 69.90% −0.7% 25.60% 74.40% 4.50% Client 29.30% 70.70% −0.9% 25.40% 74.60% 4.00% Desktop 29.90% 70.10% −5.1% 33.60% 66.40% −3.7% Mobile 29.20% 70.80% 0.20% 21.90% 78.10% 7.20% Server 35.50% 64.50% 1.00% 27.80% 72.20% 7.70% All CPUs, including IoT and SoCs 33.90% 66.10% −0.2% 30.90% 69.10% 3.00% CPU unit sales head south, set to get worseThe overall CPU market contracted both sequentially and year-over-year in unit shipments in Q3 2026, after a much stronger-than-expected second quarter, according to Mercury Research. AMD and Intel shipped 60.8 million client CPUs and 8.13 million data center processors during the quarter. One thing to keep in mind about the reports from JPR and Mercury Research is that they count CPU shipments, which happen months before those CPUs are sold in actual systems."After a far better than expected second quarter market for client processors, the third quarter PC CPU market declined far more than expected, entirely due to a downturn in mobile CPUs — this was the same segment that was unexpectedly higher last quarter, hinting that part of the downturn may have been due to CPU demand pulling in sales from the third quarter," said Dean McCarron, principal analyst at Mercury Research.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: "Both Intel and AMD indicated in their earnings results that there was a rapid softening in PC demand late in the third quarter that impacted client processor shipments and that the outlook for client CPUs in the fourth quarter will be a decline in excess of 20%. Unlike client CPUs, however, server processors continued to grow strongly in the past quarter, as did embedded CPUs." (Image credit: Mercury Research)Quarter over quarter, the decline was driven primarily by significantly lower demand for mobile processors, as 86 notebook CPU shipments dropped by more than 10%. By contrast, desktop CPU shipments recovered, largely thanks to Intel, while server and embedded CPU shipments continued to grow strongly. Excluding IoT, semi-custom SoCs, and embedded products, both AMD and Intel shipped fewer x86 processors than in the previous quarter, though AMD's decline was larger than Intel's. You may like Desktop CPU shipments crater 20% amid high component costs, but AMD gains record share despite 'ugly' desktop processor market Intel shifts production capacity from consumer to server CPUs in face of 'unprecedented' AI demand AMD expects to outsell Intel in Q4 for the first time in history Compared with the third quarter of 2025, CPU shipments declined across all major market segments except servers. Desktop and notebook CPU shipments decreased due to weaker PC demand amid rising component costs, particularly memory prices. Embedded processor and semi-custom SoC shipments also declined, primarily due to AMD's shrinking game console business. By contrast, fueled by the ongoing buildout of AI infrastructure, server CPU shipments increased by more than 20% YoY, their highest annual growth rate in nearly five years."Client CPU shipments softened in Q3 as OEMs kept inventories lean and the DIY channel remained weak," said Dr. Jon Peddie, president of Jon Peddie Research. "Server CPUs continued growing, with AMD gaining share and AI-related demand supporting the market. We expect PC conditions to remain difficult into the first half of 2027."Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsDue to weakness in the client PC space, AMD's overall x86 market share (excluding embedded and semi-custom SoC) declined by 0.6% QoQ for the first time in years, but still grew by a significant 4.5% YoY, according to Mercury Research.Client CPUs: AMD loses share for the first time since 2022In the x86 client PC segment, Intel regained some ground on AMD in Q3 2026 as overall client CPU shipments declined more sharply than expected, according to both Jon Peddie Research and Mercury Research. JPR estimates that AMD and Intel shipped 60.8 million client processors in Q3 2026, down from 62.93 million a quarter before and roughly 65 million in Q3 2025. (Image credit: Mercury Research)AMD's client CPU unit share dropped to 29.3%, down from a record 30.3% in Q2, but still notably higher than the 25.4% it commanded a year earlier. Meanwhile, Intel increased its share to 70.7%, though its position remained considerably weaker than in Q3 2025, when it controlled 74.6% of the market. What to read next Two Intel chips break Amazon's top 10 CPUs for the first time in months Intel reportedly set to hike CPU prices by 10% ahead of 'major annual product' launch in March 2027 Intel vs AMD: Which CPUs Are Better in 2026? Intel's sequential market share gains were driven entirely by a substantial increase in desktop CPU shipments, while AMD continued to gain ground in notebooks, albeit at a much slower pace than in previous quarters. Mercury Research believes that weaker demand for mobile CPUs may have enabled Intel to allocate more silicon to desktop processors, a market that the company had undersupplied for some time.However, the outlook for both companies' client CPU businesses is rather gloomy, as rising component costs (especially DRAM and 3D NAND prices) are weighing on PC demand. Both AMD and Intel anticipate a sequential decline in client CPU shipments of more than 20% in the fourth quarter and further declines in the year to come. Meanwhile, one has to keep in mind that CPUs sold in Q4 are meant for systems to be shipped in Q1, which is traditionally weak. Hence, while the 20% YoY decline is extraordinary, a substantial part of that decline is seasonal.Desktop CPUs: Intel is bringing vengeanceIn the desktop PC segment, Intel made a spectacular comeback in Q3 2026, reclaiming 5% of the market in one quarter. Intel's desktop CPU unit share climbed to 70.1%, up 5% sequentially and 3.7% in the same quarter a year ago. By contrast, AMD's share dropped to 29.9%, down from 34.9% in Q2 2026 and 33.6% in Q3 2025, meaning the company wiped out its market share gains over the past year. (Image credit: Mercury Research)Mercury Research speculates that weaker demand for notebook processors enabled Intel to allocate more silicon to mainstream desktop CPUs, a market that both companies have underserved for some time. Another factor behind AMD's poor performance was its greater exposure to the gaming PC market, which suffered from limited availability of gaming graphics cards and unusually high costs for other components, such as memory modules and SSDs.Yet, desktops became the only major x86 CPU market segment where AMD lost unit share both sequentially and year-over-year.Mobile CPUs: AMD gains amid market declinesIn the mobile PC segment, both AMD and Intel saw a substantial decline in CPU shipments in Q3 2026 as the market contracted more than 10% sequentially, according to Mercury Research. However, AMD's shipments declined slightly less than Intel's, which enabled the company to increase its mobile CPU unit share to a record 29.2%, up from 28.9% in Q2 2026 and 21.9% in Q3 2025. Intel remained the dominant supplier with a 70.8% share, down from 71.1% in the previous quarter and 78.1% a year earlier. (Image credit: Mercury Research)Although AMD's sequential market share gain of 0.2% was negligible, its 7.2% YoY gain was impressive, especially given Intel's historically strong position in the notebook market. Mercury Research attributes the sharp sequential decline in mobile CPU shipments partly to PC makers pulling forward their CPU procurements into the unusually strong second quarter.Unfortunately for both AMD and Intel, the outlook for the fourth quarter is gloomy, as rising memory and other component prices drive up notebook prices and reduce end-user demand.Server CPUs: Best quarter ever?Unlike the bleak client CPU market, server CPUs are thriving, with shipments of data center processors reaching 8.13 million units in Q3 2026, according to Jon Peddie Research. The market again grew 20% year-over-year, the highest annual growth rate in nearly five years, according to Mercury Research.In the server CPU segment, AMD continued its winning spree as its unit share reached a record 35.5%, up from 34.5% in Q2 2026 and 27.8% in Q3 2025. Intel remained the dominant supplier with a 64.5% share, down 1% sequentially and 7.7% year-over-year. (Image credit: Mercury Research)Interestingly, Intel managed to slow AMD's advance in the core data center CPU market by apparently substantially increasing shipments of its Xeon SP processors, McCarron believes. When the comparison is limited to AMD's EPYC and Intel's Xeon SP processors, AMD's unit share reached 46.8%, up just 0.4% sequentially, which represents AMD's smallest sequential gain over the past year, as the company's quarterly share gains by this metric averaged 3% over the preceding three quarters.Unlike the client CPU market, the outlook for the server processor market remains particularly favorable for both AMD and Intel. The ongoing buildout of AI infrastructure drives demand not only for conventional data center-grade processors, but also for workstation-class CPUs used in smaller departmental AI servers.SummaryShipments of x86 CPUs declined both sequentially and year-over-year in Q3 2026 to 68.93 million units as rising component prices weighed on client PC demand, while server CPU shipments grew more than 20% year-over-year.Intel regained overall x86 CPU market share from AMD for the first time since Q2 2025, largely thanks to a spectacular comeback in the desktop CPU segment, where its share reached 70.1%. Meanwhile, AMD gained 0.3% of the mobile CPU market, now commanding 29.2%, its highest share ever. Furthermore, AMD reached a record unit share in the server CPU segment, where it now commands 35.5%.Both companies expect client CPU shipments to drop by more than 20% sequentially in Q4, whereas demand for server processors continues to grow due to the ongoing buildout of AI infrastructure. items.titleZh: 英特尔自2025年以来首次夺回CPU整体市场份额
items.descriptionZh:
根据Mercury Research和Jon Peddie Research最新报告，2026年第三季度全球x86 CPU出货量为6893万颗，环比和同比均出现下滑，主要原因是组件价格高企、尤其是内存价格上升，导致客户端PC需求明显走弱；与之形成鲜明对比的是，服务器CPU出货量同比增长约20%，成为近五年来增长最强劲的细分市场。报告统计的是CPU出货量，而CPU通常要数月后才随整机售出，因此这一数据反映的是产业链提前备货和需求预期的变化，而非终端零售销量的即时变化。

从整体市场格局看，Intel自2025年第二季度以来首次从AMD手中夺回整体x86 CPU市场份额。2026年第三季度，AMD整体x86份额为30.10%，Intel为69.90%；AMD环比下降0.7个百分点，但同比仍增长4.5个百分点。若剔除IoT、半定制SoC和嵌入式产品，AMD整体x86份额环比下降0.6%，为多年来首次环比下滑，但同比仍增长4.5%。Intel本季度整体份额回升，主要来自桌面PC CPU出货的意外强劲表现；AMD则在移动和服务器CPU领域继续创下纪录。

客户端CPU市场明显承压。第三季度AMD和Intel合计出货约6080万颗客户端CPU，低于上一季度的6293万颗和2025年同期的约6500万颗。移动处理器需求下降是环比下滑的主因，笔记本CPU出货环比降幅超过10%；桌面CPU出货则有所恢复，主要由Intel带动；服务器和嵌入式CPU继续强劲增长。同比来看，除服务器外，桌面、笔记本、嵌入式和半定制SoC出货均下降。桌面和笔记本CPU下滑源于PC需求疲软及组件成本上升，尤其是内存价格；嵌入式和半定制SoC下降则主要因为AMD游戏主机业务收缩。

在客户端CPU细分市场，AMD份额降至29.3%，低于2026年第二季度创纪录的30.3%，但仍高于2025年同期的25.4%；Intel份额升至70.7%，但明显低于2025年同期的74.6%。Intel的环比份额提升完全来自桌面CPU出货大幅增加，AMD则在笔记本市场继续取得份额增长，只是速度较此前几个季度明显放缓。Mercury Research认为，移动CPU需求疲弱可能使Intel将更多晶圆产能分配给桌面处理器，而这一市场此前较长时间存在供应不足。

桌面CPU成为本季度最引人关注的变化。Intel桌面CPU份额升至70.1%，环比提高5个百分点，同比提高3.7个百分点，实现明显反弹；AMD桌面份额降至29.9%，低于2026年第二季度的34.9%和2025年同期的33.6%，过去一年的份额增益被基本抹去。桌面也是AMD唯一一个环比和同比均失去份额的主要x86 CPU细分市场。报告认为，笔记本处理器需求偏弱使Intel得以向主流桌面CPU分配更多硅片；同时，AMD对游戏PC市场暴露度更高，而游戏显卡供应有限、内存模组和SSD等组件成本异常高，也对其桌面业务造成拖累。

移动CPU方面，第三季度市场环比收缩超过10%，AMD和Intel出货均大幅下降，但AMD降幅略小于Intel，使其移动CPU份额升至创纪录的29.2%，高于2026年第二季度的28.9%和2025年同期的21.9%；Intel仍以70.8%的份额占据主导，但低于上一季度的71.1%和2025年同期的78.1%。AMD环比仅提升0.2个百分点，增幅有限，但同比提升7.2个百分点，在Intel传统强势的笔记本市场表现突出。Mercury Research认为，移动CPU出货环比大幅下降，部分原因是PC厂商将采购提前到了异常强劲的第二季度。展望第四季度，内存及其他组件涨价将推高笔记本价格并抑制终端需求，AMD和Intel均预计客户端CPU出货环比下降超过20%。

服务器CPU市场则延续高景气。2026年第三季度数据中心处理器出货量达到813万颗，同比增长超过20%，为近五年最高年增速，主要受AI基础设施持续建设推动。AMD服务器CPU份额达到创纪录的35.5%，高于2026年第二季度的34.5%和2025年同期的27.8%；Intel份额为64.5%，环比下降1个百分点，同比下降7.7个百分点。Mercury Research分析师认为，Intel通过大幅增加Xeon SP处理器出货，似乎减缓了AMD在核心数据中心CPU市场的推进。若仅比较AMD EPYC与Intel Xeon SP，AMD份额为46.8%，环比仅提升0.4个百分点，为其过去一年最小季度环比增幅，此前三个季度该指标平均每季提升约3个百分点。

整体来看，x86 CPU市场正呈现明显的结构性分化：受内存等组件涨价和PC需求转弱影响，客户端CPU出货下滑，且两家公司均预计第四季度环比降幅超过20%，PC市场困难局面可能延续至2027年上半年；服务器CPU则受益于AI数据中心建设，不仅传统数据中心级处理器需求旺盛，用于小型部门级AI服务器的工作站级CPU也获得拉动。竞争格局上，Intel凭借桌面CPU强劲反弹夺回整体份额，AMD则在移动和服务器市场继续扩大同比优势并创下份额纪录。

items.content: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on Jensen Huang’s resignation and the fallout from Nvidia’s leadership crisis, follow Terrence O’Brien. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here.How it startedOn October 29th, The New York Times reported that Nvidia co-founder and showman CEO Jensen Huang appeared to be the target of a Chinese spy plot. Any major tech CEO potentially being compromised by the Chinese government is concerning — especially Jensen Huang. “If you could draw the network diagram of the entire US AI ecosystem, Nvidia would be at the center of that,” Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, previously told The Verge. “If you could draw the diagram of the entire Nvidia ecosystem, a single man is standing at the heart of all of that.”The Times reported that Jensen Huang had developed a “close relationship” with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. Alice Huang had been on the American government’s radar for some time, perhaps as early as 2024. Her company was investigated by the US Commerce Department over suspicions it was illegally smuggling Nvidia’s AI chips into China in violation of US government trade restrictions. Singapore authorities confiscated her passport back in June of 2025, eventually barring her from the country, after she reportedly gave “inaccurate information” to police. And perhaps more concerningly, some US officials believed she was passing information, possibly about Nvidia’s designs or the White House’s deliberations over trade restrictions, directly back to Beijing.This made her relationship with Jensen Huang concerning for multiple reasons. Nvidia’s chips are considered crucial to America’s AI superiority and a matter of national security by the White House. The government has restricted the sale of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China since the Biden administration. But Jensen Huang has routinely pushed to loosen those trade restrictions. Meanwhile, he had gotten quite cozy with President Trump, once even putting him on speakerphone on-stage at the All-In Summit.Then last week, things escalated quickly.On Friday, November 6th, the Times reported that Alice Huang was specifically recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO. Though, there is some disagreement among US intelligence officials over the strength of evidence tying Alice Huang to Beijing. While the paper did not confirm it at the time, rumors suggested the “close relationship” between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang was romantic in nature.On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair, but did not name the Megaspeed exec and alleged Chinese spy specifically. Nvidia’s board announced that it was launching an investigation into its CEO shortly after.Many believed that Jensen Huang would survive the scandal. His company’s importance to America’s booming AI industry and his crucial role at the company seemed to make him nearly untouchable. He was, after all, the only CEO the company had ever known with no clear and obvious succession plan in place, and he sat atop an unusual corporate structure with around 60 direct reports. (These numbers are slightly outdated, but according to the Harvard Business Review, 10 to 20 is far more common among Fortune 500 companies, and Tim Cook reportedly had 17 in 2015, which was deemed “a lot” by Business Insider.)Then on Wednesday, November 11th, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had a second affair — this one with one of his direct reports, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. Whether that was the last straw or if they were afraid it would be merely the tip of the iceberg, the board was ready to push Jensen Huang out, according to reports circulating that evening. According to Bloomberg, he had accepted his fate Wednesday evening reportedly looking “broken and shattered” and telling people, “I’m a piece of shit.”On Thursday, November 12th, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO of Nvidia.How it’s goingCFO Colette Kress was immediately named interim CEO, and acknowledged to employees that this has been an “extraordinarily difficult period.” Harvey Jones was also named the first board chair in the company’s history, already signaling there would be some changes to the corporate structure. In a memo to employees, Jones said the company would “search for a permanent successor looking at both internal and external candidates.”But the destabilizing impact was immediate. Nvidia’s stock closed at an all-time high of $239.24 on October 6th. It closed at $162.85 on November 13th. It’s hard to overstate the importance of Nvidia to the US’s AI arms race with China, and the industry in general. The company has invested $99 billion in various AI labs, startups, and neo clouds. Plus has announced plans to mobilize over $500 billion in financing for building out AI data centers and other infrastructure.Even before Jensen Huang had resigned, Nvidia was already facing a shareholder lawsuit claiming the company had deceived investors. Jensen Huang and the company’s spokespeople insisted that the relationship with Alice Huang and Megaspeed was “completely normal and not unusual.” Only days later, Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair that raised “national security concerns” without naming anyone specifically. According to Reuters, Jensen Huang misled several Nvidia leaders, “including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld” about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang.Many in the AI industry and Silicon Valley jumped to Jensen Huang’s defense. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney called it a “sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity,” in a particularly hyperbolic post. Elon Musk said on X that it would “be an honor” to hire Jensen Huang. Many of Nvidia’s employees even voiced their support to “bring back THE boss,” on an internal post.Some even speculated that Jensen Huang was the victim of a vast conspiracy, whether that was a coup by some faction within Nvidia, or perhaps the goal of China all along had simply been to chase him from the CEO chair.By Thursday night, Reuters reported a third affair, this one also with an Nvidia employee, though no further information has emerged.What happens nextFirst and foremost for Nvidia, it must find a new CEO. It’s possible that Kress eventually ceases to be “interim” CEO, but other names, including Apple’s hardware chief Johny Srouji, have also been rumored. (Donald Trump believes they should hire Tim Cook, but to call that unlikely would be an understatement.)It’s also possible that Nvidia will undergo a dramatic reorganization. Whoever takes over as CEO is unlikely to keep the 60 direct reports of Jensen Huang. With a first-ever board chair in Jones, it’s also possible that the board of directors will play a larger role in the company going forward.The board’s investigation into Jensen Huang that began on November 8th is ongoing. The scandal is likely to drag on for some time. With the possibility that Jensen Huang will have to testify before Congress, the company may choose to be proactive about disclosing any additional information publicly.The incoming Democratic majority is expected to come down harder on Silicon Valley than the current Republican Congress. While it’s unclear just how far the new House and Senate will go in trying to rein in the tech industry and its billionaire leaders, it’s possible it will try to make an example of Nvidia as an early act of strength. If Nvidia is found to have been turning a blind eye to companies like Megaspeed, which are suspected of funneling advanced chips to China, it could face civil or criminal penalties. And it seems increasingly likely that stricter trade restrictions will be implemented on Nvidia’s chips, which could increase tensions with China in an already costly trade war.There is a possibility that Jensen Huang could face criminal charges. In May, he claimed that Nvidia had “zero percent” market share in China due to stringent export restrictions. But shortly after, Culper Research published a report claiming that in reality over 20 percent of the company’s 2026 compute revenue was from China, though that number has not been independently verified. The report cited “illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries” as the primary source of those revenues. Among the largest of those intermediaries, according to Culper Research, was Megaspeed, which Nvidia repeatedly vouched for to the US government.If proof is established that the CEO was knowingly helping Megaspeed or any other companies to illegally divert restricted chips to China, he could face criminal charges. And, as The Verge’s Elizabeth Lopatto put it, “under a functioning legal system, [he] could actually go to jail.”There is the chance that members of the current administration are also tied up in this scandal, as it’s unclear how much the White House knew and when.Considering Nvidia’s sizable investments, borrowing to build data centers, and the importance of its hardware, there are tons of open questions about how this impacts not just the AI industry, but the American economy as a whole. Nvidia is essentially propping up a large part of the tech industry and, if money stops flowing out of its coffers, it could drag a lot of other companies down with it.There are also open questions about how this impacts the American public’s perception of the AI industry. The new Democratic majority was elected in part by campaigning against AI companies and the explosion of data center buildout across the country. That one of its more prominent CEOs is now embroiled in a spying scandal and multiple extramarital affairs probably isn’t going to endear the industry to the public.By the wayMegaspeed was the largest buyer of Nvidia chips in Southeast Asia, but when Singaporean newspaper The Straits Times visited its office in October of 2025, it found “no signs of activity.”Megaspeed is just one of multiple companies that Nvidia has been approved to sell chips with suspicious offices. The New York Times described New Matrix’s headquarters as “a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be.”Jensen Huang’s connections to Super Micro are also under scrutiny. Earlier this year, one of its founders, an employee, and a contractor for the company were indicted by the Justice Department for conspiring to violate American export controls and divert Nvidia chips to China.Read thisWhile a lot has changed, it’s still worth reading the Times’ first big report from October 29th that lays the groundwork for the eventual deluge of international intrigue and infidelity that ultimately led to Jensen Huang’s downfall.The New York Times paints a fascinating portrait of Alice Huang who now finds herself at the center of an international espionage scandal.The Decoder interview with Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, digs into what China hoped to get out of Jensen Huang.

items.descriptionZh:
这是一则关于英伟达CEO黄仁勋因间谍丑闻和婚外情曝光而辞职的深度报道。以下是完整中文摘要：

---

**事件背景与起因**

2025年10月29日，《纽约时报》报道称，英伟达联合创始人兼CEO黄仁勋疑似成为中国间谍行动的目标。任何大型科技公司CEO若可能被中国政府渗透都令人担忧，而黄仁勋的情况尤为敏感。布鲁金斯学会约翰·桑顿中国中心外交政策研究员凯尔·陈此前对The Verge表示：“如果你画出整个美国AI生态系统的网络图，英伟达处于中心位置。如果你画出整个英伟达生态系统的图，一个人站在所有这一切的核心。”

据报道，黄仁勋与新加坡数据中心公司Megaspeed的高管Alice Huang（与黄仁勋无亲属关系）发展了“密切关系”。Alice Huang早已进入美国政府视野，最早可能追溯到2024年。她的公司因涉嫌违反美国贸易限制、非法向中国走私英伟达AI芯片而受到美国商务部调查。2025年6月，新加坡当局没收了她的护照，最终禁止其入境，原因是她向警方提供了“不准确信息”。更令人担忧的是，部分美国官员认为她正在将信息——可能涉及英伟达的设计方案或白宫关于贸易限制的讨论——直接传递给北京。

这段关系之所以令人不安有多重原因。白宫将英伟达芯片视为美国AI优势的关键和国家安全的组成部分。自拜登政府以来，美国一直限制向中国出售英伟达最先进的芯片。但黄仁勋屡次推动放松这些贸易限制，同时与特朗普总统关系密切，甚至曾在All-In Summit峰会上将特朗普的电话接通并在台上免提播放。

**事件升级与辞职经过**

11月6日（周五），《纽约时报》报道称Alice Huang系被中国国家安全部专门招募来监视英伟达CEO。不过，美国情报官员对将Alice Huang与北京关联的证据强度存在分歧。虽然当时报纸未证实，但传言称黄仁勋与Alice Huang的“密切关系”具有恋爱性质。

11月8日（周日），黄仁勋承认有一段婚外情，但未点名Megaspeed高管或所谓的中国间谍。英伟达董事会随即宣布对其CEO展开调查。

许多人认为黄仁勋能够挺过这场丑闻。他公司对美国蓬勃发展的AI产业至关重要，他在公司的核心角色似乎使他几乎不可撼动。毕竟，他是公司历史上唯一的CEO，没有明确的后继计划，而且他管理着一种不寻常的公司结构，拥有约60名直接下属。（这一数字略有过时，但据《哈佛商业评论》统计，财富500强公司中10到20名直接下属更为常见，据报道蒂姆·库克2015年有17名直接下属，已被《商业内幕》视为“很多”。）

11月11日（周三），《纽约时报》报道黄仁勋有第二段婚外情——这次对象是他的直接下属、英伟达医疗健康业务副总裁Kimberly Powell。无论这是压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，还是董事会担心这仅仅是冰山一角，据当晚流传的报道，董事会已准备将黄仁勋逐出。据彭博社报道，他在周三晚间接受了命运，据报道看起来“破碎而崩溃”，并对人说：“我是个废物。”

11月12日（周四），英伟达宣布黄仁勋辞去CEO职务。

**辞职后的连锁反应**

CFO科莱特·克雷斯被立即任命为临时CEO，并向员工承认这是一段“极其艰难的时期”。哈维·琼斯被任命为公司历史上首位董事会主席，这已表明公司结构将有所变化。琼斯在致员工的备忘录中表示，公司将“在内部和外部候选人中寻找永久继任者”。

但 destabilizing 影响立竿见影。英伟达股价10月6日收于历史高点239.24美元，11月13日收于162.85美元。英伟达对美国与中国AI军备竞赛以及整个行业的重要性怎么强调都不为过。该公司已向各类AI实验室、初创企业和新型云服务商投资990亿美元，并宣布计划动员超过5000亿美元融资用于建设AI数据中心和其他基础设施。

早在黄仁勋辞职之前，英伟达已面临股东诉讼，指控公司欺骗投资者。黄仁勋和公司发言人坚称与Alice Huang和Megaspeed的关系“完全正常、并无异常”。仅数天后，黄仁勋承认有一段引发“国家安全担忧”的婚外情，但未具体点名任何人。据路透社报道，黄仁勋在Alice Huang关系性质上误导了多名英伟达高管，“包括总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特和首席营销官艾莉森·瓦根菲尔德”。

AI行业和硅谷许多人跳出来为黄仁勋辩护。Epic Games CEO蒂姆·斯威尼发表尤为夸张的帖子称这是“对英伟达、开发者、美国和全人类的悲伤一天”。埃隆·马斯克在X上表示雇佣黄仁勋“将是一种荣誉”。许多英伟达员工甚至在内部帖子中发声支持“让老板回来”。

一些人甚至猜测黄仁勋是一场巨大阴谋的受害者——无论是英伟达内部某个派系发动的政变，还是中国从一开始就只是想把他从CEO位置上赶走。到周四晚间，路透社报道了第三段婚外情，同样涉及一名英伟达员工，但未披露更多信息。

**后续走向与潜在影响**

首先，英伟达必须找到新CEO。克雷斯有可能最终去掉“临时”头衔，但其他名字也在流传，包括苹果硬件主管约翰尼·斯鲁吉。（特朗普认为应该聘请蒂姆·库克，但这几乎不可能。）英伟达也可能进行大规模重组。无论谁接任CEO，都不太可能保留黄仁勋的60名直接下属。随着琼斯成为首位董事会主席，董事会未来可能发挥更大作用。

董事会自11月8日启动的对黄仁勋的调查仍在进行中。丑闻可能持续一段时间。由于黄仁勋可能需要在国会作证，公司可能选择主动公开披露更多信息。

即将上任的民主党多数派预计将比现任共和党国会更严厉地对待硅谷。虽然尚不清楚新一届众议院和参议院将在多大程度上试图约束科技行业及其亿万富翁领袖，但有可能拿英伟达开刀以展示力量。如果英伟达被认定对Megaspeed等涉嫌向中国输送先进芯片的公司视而不见，可能面临民事或刑事处罚。对英伟达芯片实施更严格的贸易限制似乎越来越可能，这可能在已然代价高昂的贸易战中加剧与中国的紧张关系。

黄仁勋可能面临刑事指控。今年5月，他声称由于严格的出口限制，英伟达在中国市场份额为“零”。但不久后，Culper Research发布报告称，实际上公司2026年计算收入的20%以上来自中国，尽管该数字未经独立核实。报告将“非法GPU转移和东南亚中间商”列为这些收入的主要来源。据Culper Research称，其中最大的中间商之一就是英伟达多次向美国政府担保的Megaspeed。如果证实CEO明知故犯地帮助Megaspeed或其他公司非法向中国转移受限芯片，他可能面临刑事指控。正如The Verge的伊丽莎白·洛帕托所言，“在一个正常运转的法律体系下，他实际上可能入狱。”

现任政府成员也可能卷入这场丑闻，因为尚不清楚白宫知道多少以及何时知道。考虑到英伟达的巨额投资、为建设数据中心而进行的借贷以及其硬件的重要性，这一事件对AI行业乃至美国经济整体影响存在大量未解问题。英伟达本质上支撑着科技行业的一大部分，如果资金停止从其金库流出，可能会拖累许多其他公司。

美国公众对AI行业的看法也面临不确定性。新当选的民主党多数派部分正是通过反对AI公司和全国数据中心建设热潮而当选的。其最知名的CEO之一如今深陷间谍丑闻和多段婚外情，恐怕不会让该行业更受公众欢迎。

**补充细节**

Megaspeed是英伟达芯片在东南亚的最大买家，但新加坡《海峡时报》2025年10月探访其办公室时发现“没有任何活动迹象”。Megaspeed只是英伟达获准向其销售芯片的众多可疑办公室公司之一。《纽约时报》将New Matrix总部描述为“一个空心的灰色外壳，天花板上本应装灯的地方垂着电线”。黄仁勋与超微电脑的关联也受到审视。今年早些时候，该公司一名创始人、一名员工和一名承包商被司法部起诉，罪名是合谋违反美国出口管制并将英伟达芯片转移至中国。

history.content: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The latest edition of our Stepback newsletter should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning. That includes rumors that Jensen Huang might be trying to find a path back to CEO, and a statement from Megaspeed claiming that Alice Huang hasn’t worked for the company since August of 2025, which raises more questions than it answers.Some big names, including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have publicly thrown their support behind a public letter demanding Nvidia “bring Jensen back.”The public letter calling for Jensen Huang to be reinstated has over 150,000 signatures, but it’s difficult to verify their authenticity. Business Insider reports that signatures include “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor” and “Xi Jingping,” likely a misspelling of Chinese president Xi Jinping.The Financial Times reports that Jensen Huang has discussed the possibility of returning as CEO with close allies, as some Silicon Valley insiders and employees attempt to pressure the board.Not all believe Jensen Huang should be allowed to return to his seat. According to the Financial Times, one ally acknowledged that, “Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense.”23andMe founder Anne Wojcicki told Bloomberg that “Power corrupts, and people start to think they are invincible … We are all complicit in making these people think they are gods. And people do stupid things when they think they are untouchable.”Wojcicki endured a messy public divorce from Google co-founder Sergey Brin, after it was revealed he was having an affair with an employee.According to Bloomberg, many women in Silicon Valley see Jensen Huang as simply another example of a rich man abusing their position and “leveraging power to pursue sexual relationships with their employees.”Megaspeed released a statement saying that Alice Huang left the company “effective Aug. 30, 2025, and currently has no role with the company,” adding that “Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters.”

history.descriptionZh:
这篇英文报道聚焦英伟达（Nvidia）联合创始人、前CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）的复职风波，属于公司治理、高管丑闻与硅谷权力文化新闻，而非AI芯片技术发布。原文未涉及芯片架构、制程、算力、带宽、能效、性能对比或应用场景等技术信息，因此无法从中提取核心技术原理和创新点；以下摘要集中梳理事件背景、各方表态及其可能影响。

事件正在快速演变。Stepback newsletter最新一期原本用于帮助读者了解背景，但自当天上午以来又出现多项新进展：有传闻称黄仁勋可能正试图寻找重返CEO职位的路径；Megaspeed则发表声明称，Alice Huang自2025年8月30日起已离开公司，目前在公司没有任何角色，并称公司不对其个人和私人事务置评。报道认为，这一声明反而引发更多疑问，而非解答问题。

公众层面，一封要求英伟达“让Jensen回来”的公开信已获得超过15万个签名，但签名真实性难以核实。Business Insider报道称，签名者中出现“Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor”和“Xi Jingping”等署名，后者很可能是中国国家主席习近平英文名的拼写错误，显示签名列表存在明显不可信或恶搞成分。尽管如此，埃隆·马斯克和Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney等知名人物已公开支持这封公开信。

据《金融时报》报道，黄仁勋已与亲密盟友讨论过重返CEO职位的可能性，同时一些硅谷内部人士和员工正试图向董事会施压。不过，并非所有人都认为应允许他回归。报道援引一名盟友的话称，“与下属发生婚外情是可被解雇的行为”。23andMe创始人Anne Wojcicki对彭博社表示，“权力会腐蚀人，人们开始觉得自己不可战胜……我们都在让这些人以为自己像神一样。当人们觉得自己不可触碰时，就会做蠢事。”Wojcicki曾与谷歌联合创始人Sergey Brin经历一场公开而混乱的离婚，此前Brin被曝与一名员工有婚外情。彭博社还称，许多硅谷女性将黄仁勋视为富人滥用职位、“利用权力追求与员工发生性关系”的又一例证。

整体来看，该事件的核心争议包括：黄仁勋是否应重返CEO、董事会将如何应对内部员工和外部公众压力、公开信签名真实性与舆论操纵问题，以及高管与下属之间的权力不对等和公司治理风险。对公司层面而言，领导层稳定性、声誉和战略执行可能受到影响；但原文没有提供任何AI芯片技术参数、产品路线图或可量化业务数据，因此无法据此评估技术性能或应用影响。

history.content: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also sent letters to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the committee.Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act, first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are receiving renewed interest. While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters. Johnson has also said that he personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful AI chips from companies like Nvidia.RelatedAn overview of Jensen Huang’s messy daysJensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO

history.titleZh: 美国国会拟在英伟达间谍丑闻后收紧AI芯片出口规定
history.descriptionZh:
报道称，在英伟达前CEO黄仁勋卷入与一名疑似中国间谍有关的丑闻后，美国国会正寻求进一步限制AI芯片出口。文章将黄仁勋称为“现已卸任”的英伟达CEO，并称民主党和共和党都支持收紧规则的多项措施和法案，同时要求黄仁勋及其他英伟达高层赴国会作证。参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默表示，黄仁勋和特朗普政府需要向国会作出交代；参议院银行委员会主席蒂姆·斯科特已分别致信黄仁勋和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克，要求他们公开到该委员会作证。

立法层面，2025年4月首次在众议院提出、后在参议院停滞的《远程访问安全法案》重新受到关注。原文未展开该法案具体条款，但从名称看，其重点涉及远程访问安全，可能与堵塞通过远程方式获取受出口管制技术或算力的漏洞有关。报道同时指出，该具体法案未必最终成为法律，但众议院议长迈克·约翰逊称，国会内部对限制对华芯片出口“正在形成越来越大的共识”，并称他个人支持限制中国获取英伟达等公司的强大AI芯片。

从背景看，AI芯片是训练和运行大模型、建设数据中心和高性能计算集群的关键硬件，美国近年来一直通过出口管制限制中国获得高端GPU和AI加速器。此次报道的核心不是某一款芯片的架构、制程、算力或带宽等性能参数，而是政治与监管风险：一场涉及黄仁勋和疑似中国间谍的丑闻，正在把英伟达及AI芯片出口问题推向国会听证和立法博弈。若国会进一步收紧出口规则，可能影响英伟达对华业务、AI芯片供应链以及中国获取高端算力的渠道；同时，国会要求高管作证也意味着企业面临更强的公开问责和政治压力。文章相关链接还提到“黄仁勋混乱的日子”以及“有远见的表演型创始人CEO的衰落”，显示该报道将个人丑闻、公司治理与AI芯片出口管制政策联系在一起。原文未提供具体技术原理、创新点或对比性能数据。

history.description: Dai's post shows how much Nvidia employees looked up to the former CEO.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Just days after Jensen Huang suddenly resigned from his position at Nvidia, an Nvidia Robot Research Engineer said that he would leave the company as well. But more than just showing support for the former CEO with a generic “I stand with Jensen” message, Darrel Dai laid out several reasons for the decision on X.I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say. As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO. I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI. I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in. But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build. Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard. That is why this has been so disappointing. I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny. What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me. I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected. I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day. A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too. Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close. I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me. These are my personal views.November 15, 2026“What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me,” the engineer posted. “I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.”It seems that Jensen Huang has gained the respect of the people working under him, with many calling for his reinstatement despite the many controversies he is currently facing. There’s also an online petition demanding that the Nvidia board “Bring Jensen Back,” with over 150,000 signatures at the time of writing.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Nvidia is centered around Jensen Huang, with the former chief executive reportedly having a small army of 60 people directly reporting to him. But despite his busy schedule and legendary persona, Dai said that “Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly,” and that “It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.” Dai also pointed out that “employees’ trust and sense of belonging” are part of what makes a company great. More importantly, Nvidia is known as one of the tech companies with the most generous pay packages. Jensen was even quoted saying, “I pay my employees as much as I can.”It remains unclear what the former Nvidia CEO will do after all these issues. Elon Musk has already said on X that “it would be an honor” to hire Jensen Huang, especially as he’s embarking on his own ambitious chipmaking journey. As for the employees left behind at Nvidia, some are staying and have shown their full support to interim CEO Colette Kress, while many more want him back. However, there has also been talk that various Silicon Valley tech and semiconductor firms are aggressively attempting to poach Nvidians, although these are just rumors so far. history.titleZh: 英伟达工程师因黄仁勋退出缺乏透明度而离职，并详述决定
history.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware报道，在英伟达CEO黄仁勋突然辞职数日后，英伟达机器人研究工程师Darrel Dai宣布也将离开公司，并在X平台发长文说明原因。此事不只是“站队”表态，而是折射出黄仁勋辞职对英伟达内部工程师文化和员工信任的冲击。

Dai表示，他眼中的黄仁勋不只是CEO，更是愿意押注“尚未显而易见的未来”的领导者。黄仁勋在深度学习热潮到来前很久就重注CUDA，使英伟达在AI成为行业优先事项之前完成基础设施布局。CUDA的核心意义在于让GPU能够以并行方式执行通用计算任务，并通过编程模型和软件生态把开发者、AI框架与英伟达硬件连接起来，形成从训练到推理的算力平台。Dai还提到，他在“物理AI”方向看到同样的愿景：投资机器人、共享开源工具和项目、构建把AI带入物理世界的计算平台。物理AI通常指机器人、具身智能等系统在真实环境中完成感知、决策和执行，需要仿真训练、实时推理、边缘计算和软硬件协同平台。原文没有披露具体芯片型号、算力、功耗或基准对比数据，报道重点并非产品性能，而是人事变动与工程文化。

Dai尤其看重黄仁勋塑造的工程文化：鼓励工程师探索、冒险、从错误中学习；即使公司规模庞大，黄仁勋也会阅读员工的“Top 5”邮件、跟踪员工工作并直接互动，让个体工程师感到自己的想法仍能被听见。文章还提到，英伟达以薪酬慷慨著称，黄仁勋曾表示会尽可能高薪支付员工。Dai称，黄仁勋的愿景和工程文化是他愿意留在英伟达的重要原因。

对于黄仁勋辞职所涉指控，Dai表示自己没有掌握全部事实，也不预判调查，并且认为对黄的钦佩不能使其免于审查。但他难以接受的是，在尚未获得能帮助自己理解辞职的解释之前，就要接受黄离开；公司方向、文化以及具体做事的人将受到何种影响仍不清楚。他说自己一直感到工程师视角在英伟达受到重视，但在这项决定上“没有感到被听见”，这种落差比预期更痛苦。他理解部分信息不能立即分享，但这不能消除被排除在影响公司日常建设的决策之外的感觉。公司伟大来自领导力、治理以及把雄心变成现实的人，员工的信任和归属感也是其中一部分。最终，他带着悲伤和感激决定结束自己在英伟达的篇章。

报道显示，黄仁勋在部下中获得了相当尊重，许多人呼吁其复职。网上请愿要求英伟达董事会“Bring Jensen Back”，截至报道时已有超过15万签名。英伟达被认为高度围绕黄仁勋运转，据称有约60人直接向他汇报。部分员工支持临时CEO Colette Kress，但更多人希望黄仁勋回归；同时有传闻称硅谷科技和半导体公司正积极挖角英伟达员工。Elon Musk也在X上表示，雇用黄仁勋“将是一种荣幸”，尤其在他推进自己的芯片制造计划之际。整体来看，这篇报道的核心不是新技术发布，而是英伟达在创始人式CEO突然离职后，如何面对工程师文化、组织信任、人才留存和领导层过渡的不确定性。

history.title: Nvidia RTX 5090 stock returns to Newegg with 21 models
history.description: After rumors of Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards being withdrawn from the consumer retail channel it is pleasing to see major U.S. eTailers like Newegg stuffed with cheaper stock today.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter After rumors of Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards being withdrawn from the consumer retail channel, it is pleasing to see major U.S. e-tailers like Newegg stuffed with stock today. Checking out this popular online electronics retailer, we note that there are 21 RTX 5090 SKUs available, and 11 are sold by and shipped by Newegg. Sadly, pricing remains in 3x MSRP+ territory at the time of writing. Remember, you can sift through pricing trends in our comprehensive GPU price tracking 2026 feature to see that Nvidia's Blackwell flagship was once available at its fabled sub-$2,000 price. (Image credit: Newegg)Despite what looks on the surface like an ample supply (but there are order limits of one per customer), prices for RTX 5090s remain extremely high. The best prices we can see at Newegg are $6,599, but this price applies only to a water-cooled Aorus model and another sold inside a Gigabyte AI BOX eGPU. They might still appeal to you, depending on your setup, though.For a ‘standard’ air-cooled graphics card, albeit a very nice Aorus RTX 5090 Master, you’ll need to squeeze at least $6,659 out of your savings. A bonus with this card, alongside several others from the Gigabyte stables now purchasable from Newegg, is that it comes with a free motherboard. Many of these Gigabyte Aorus designs are being bundled with a full-ATX-sized X870 Aorus Elite WIFI7 AM5 motherboard, purportedly worth $319. Please note that the same motherboard is available to purchase outside this bundle for a more reasonable $249.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: If you have money to burn, there are plenty of even more expensive SKUs to pick from. There are no opulent Golden Dhabab models on Newegg, sadly, but you’ll still be asked to part with $11,896 for the Asus ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 Edition 20 (sold by a Newegg marketplace partner). Perhaps surprisingly, given recent trending pricing news, that’s the only model above $10K, but there are still many models that are almost $10,000 from Asus, MSI, and Zotac. Even an Nvidia Founders Edition RTX 5090 refurb is priced at $8,899.In context, these RTX 5090s are still at astronomical prices for consumer gaming PC add-in hardware. But they are now purchasable from a big retailer with fast delivery, rather than off a random scalper. It was only a month ago that rumors swirled about the RTX 5090 and the RTX 5080 being withdrawn from retail. That seemed to trigger crazy levels of price inflation, and reports of $10,000+ prices for the flagship card seemed to become the norm. history.titleZh: 英伟达 RTX 5090 现货重返新蛋，涵盖 21 款型号
history.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware报道，此前有传闻称Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090和RTX 5080将退出美国零售渠道，并引发旗舰显卡价格剧烈上涨，RTX 5090一度出现1万美元以上报价成为常态。如今，美国大型在线零售商Newegg重新上架了较多RTX 5090库存：共有21个SKU，其中11个由Newegg自营销售并发货，但每个客户限购一张。供应看似改善，价格却仍处于建议零售价（MSRP）3倍以上的区间，远未回归正常。

从价格看，Newegg上RTX 5090最低可见价格为6599美元，但仅适用于水冷版Aorus型号以及装在Gigabyte AI BOX外置GPU坞中的版本；标准风冷型号中，Aorus RTX 5090 Master至少需要6659美元。部分Gigabyte Aorus显卡还捆绑一块全ATX规格的X870 Aorus Elite WIFI7 AM5主板，官方称价值319美元，但该主板单独购买价格为249美元。更昂贵的选项包括由Newegg市场第三方销售的Asus ROG Astral GeForce RTX 5090 Edition 20，售价11896美元，是页面上唯一超过1万美元的型号；Asus、MSI和Zotac仍有多款接近1万美元的产品，甚至Nvidia Founders Edition RTX 5090翻新卡也标价8899美元。作为对比，Blackwell旗舰RTX 5090曾出现过低于2000美元的价格，而RTX 5080也曾被报道涨至2000美元，超过RTX 5090首发价且库存有限；Nvidia商店还曾撤下RTX 5080和RTX 5090商品页面。

技术层面，RTX 5090是Nvidia Blackwell架构的消费级旗舰显卡，主要面向高端游戏PC、内容创作、AI推理和小型工作站等场景；水冷版、风冷版以及AI BOX外置GPU方案的区别主要在散热形态和系统集成方式，而非本文重点讨论的规格性能。此次新闻的核心并非新硬件发布，而是高端GPU零售渠道的供需失衡：Newegg恢复库存和限购措施有助于抑制部分黄牛与第三方加价，但当前价格仍显著偏离MSRP，捆绑主板和eGPU套装也提高了实际购买门槛。若Newegg及其他渠道的库存持续流入，RTX 5090和RTX 5080价格有望逐步回落；否则，高端游戏与AI工作站用户的升级成本仍将维持高位。

history.title: Intel reclaims overall CPU market share for the first time since 2025
history.description: AMD continues to gain server CPU market share amid skyrocketing shipments of data center processors as sales of client CPUs drop in the third quarter, says Mercury Research.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Shipments of x86 CPUs declined quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year in the third quarter as demand for client processors dropped sharply due to high component prices, while server CPU unit sales grew by a whopping 20% year-over-year, according to the latest report from Mercury Research. Intel regained overall CPU market share from AMD for the first time since Q2 2025, largely due to surprisingly strong performance in desktop PCs. Meanwhile, AMD continued to set new records in the mobile and server CPU segments, the report claims. In total, the industry supplied 68.93 million x86 CPUs, Jon Peddie Research reports. AMD and Intel shipped 60.8 million client CPUs and 8.13 million data center processors during the quarter. One thing to keep in mind about the reports from JPR and Mercury Research is that they count CPU shipments, which happen months before those CPUs are sold in actual systems."After a far better than expected second quarter market for client processors, the third quarter PC CPU market declined far more than expected, entirely due to a downturn in mobile CPUs — this was the same segment that was unexpectedly higher last quarter, hinting that part of the downturn may have been due to CPU demand pulling in sales from the third quarter," said Dean McCarron, principal analyst at Mercury Research.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: "Both Intel and AMD indicated in their earnings results that there was a rapid softening in PC demand late in the third quarter that impacted client processor shipments and that the outlook for client CPUs in the fourth quarter will be a decline in excess of 20%. Unlike client CPUs, however, server processors continued to grow strongly in the past quarter, as did embedded CPUs." (Image credit: Mercury Research)Quarter over quarter, the decline was driven primarily by significantly lower demand for mobile processors, as 86 notebook CPU shipments dropped by more than 10%. By contrast, desktop CPU shipments recovered, largely thanks to Intel, while server and embedded CPU shipments continued to grow strongly. Excluding IoT, semi-custom SoCs, and embedded products, both AMD and Intel shipped fewer x86 processors than in the previous quarter, though AMD's decline was larger than Intel's. Desktop and notebook CPU shipments decreased due to weaker PC demand amid rising component costs, particularly memory prices. Embedded processor and semi-custom SoC shipments also declined, primarily due to AMD's shrinking game console business. By contrast, fueled by the ongoing buildout of AI infrastructure, server CPU shipments increased by more than 20% YoY, their highest annual growth rate in nearly five years."Client CPU shipments softened in Q3 as OEMs kept inventories lean and the DIY channel remained weak," said Dr. Jon Peddie, president of Jon Peddie Research. "Server CPUs continued growing, with AMD gaining share and AI-related demand supporting the market. We expect PC conditions to remain difficult into the first half of 2027."Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsDue to weakness in the client PC space, AMD's overall x86 market share (excluding embedded and semi-custom SoC) declined by 0.6% QoQ for the first time in years, but still grew by a significant 4.5% YoY, according to Mercury Research.Client CPUs: AMD loses share for the first time since 2022In the x86 client PC segment, Intel regained some ground on AMD in Q3 2026 as overall client CPU shipments declined more sharply than expected, according to both Jon Peddie Research and Mercury Research. JPR estimates that AMD and Intel shipped 60.8 million client processors in Q3 2026, down from 62.93 million a quarter before and roughly 65 million in Q3 2025. (Image credit: Mercury Research)AMD's client CPU unit share dropped to 29.3%, down from a record 30.3% in Q2, but still notably higher than the 25.4% it commanded a year earlier. Meanwhile, Intel increased its share to 70.7%, though its position remained considerably weaker than in Q3 2025, when it controlled 74.6% of the market. What to read next Two Intel chips break Amazon's top 10 CPUs for the first time in months Intel reportedly set to hike CPU prices by 10% ahead of 'major annual product' launch in March 2027 Intel vs AMD: Which CPUs Are Better in 2026? Intel's sequential market share gains were driven entirely by a substantial increase in desktop CPU shipments, while AMD continued to gain ground in notebooks, albeit at a much slower pace than in previous quarters. Mercury Research believes that weaker demand for mobile CPUs may have enabled Intel to allocate more silicon to desktop processors, a market that the company had undersupplied for some time.However, the outlook for both companies' client CPU businesses is rather gloomy, as rising component costs (especially DRAM and 3D NAND prices) are weighing on PC demand. Both AMD and Intel anticipate a sequential decline in client CPU shipments of more than 20% in the fourth quarter and further declines in the year to come. Meanwhile, one has to keep in mind that CPUs sold in Q4 are meant for systems to be shipped in Q1, which is traditionally weak. Hence, while the 20% YoY decline is extraordinary, a substantial part of that decline is seasonal.Desktop CPUs: Intel is bringing vengeanceIn the desktop PC segment, Intel made a spectacular comeback in Q3 2026, reclaiming 5% of the market in one quarter. Intel's desktop CPU unit share climbed to 70.1%, up 5% sequentially and 3.7% in the same quarter a year ago. By contrast, AMD's share dropped to 29.9%, down from 34.9% in Q2 2026 and 33.6% in Q3 2025, meaning the company wiped out its market share gains over the past year. (Image credit: Mercury Research)Mercury Research speculates that weaker demand for notebook processors enabled Intel to allocate more silicon to mainstream desktop CPUs, a market that both companies have underserved for some time. Another factor behind AMD's poor performance was its greater exposure to the gaming PC market, which suffered from limited availability of gaming graphics cards and unusually high costs for other components, such as memory modules and SSDs.Yet, desktops became the only major x86 CPU market segment where AMD lost unit share both sequentially and year-over-year.Mobile CPUs: AMD gains amid market declinesIn the mobile PC segment, both AMD and Intel saw a substantial decline in CPU shipments in Q3 2026 as the market contracted more than 10% sequentially, according to Mercury Research. However, AMD's shipments declined slightly less than Intel's, which enabled the company to increase its mobile CPU unit share to a record 29.2%, up from 28.9% in Q2 2026 and 21.9% in Q3 2025. Intel remained the dominant supplier with a 70.8% share, down from 71.1% in the previous quarter and 78.1% a year earlier. (Image credit: Mercury Research)Although AMD's sequential market share gain of 0.2% was negligible, its 7.2% YoY gain was impressive, especially given Intel's historically strong position in the notebook market. Mercury Research attributes the sharp sequential decline in mobile CPU shipments partly to PC makers pulling forward their CPU procurements into the unusually strong second quarter.Unfortunately for both AMD and Intel, the outlook for the fourth quarter is gloomy, as rising memory and other component prices drive up notebook prices and reduce end-user demand.Server CPUs: Best quarter ever?Unlike the bleak client CPU market, server CPUs are thriving, with shipments of data center processors reaching 8.13 million units in Q3 2026, according to Jon Peddie Research. The market again grew 20% year-over-year, the highest annual growth rate in nearly five years, according to Mercury Research.In the server CPU segment, AMD continued its winning spree as its unit share reached a record 35.5%, up from 34.5% in Q2 2026 and 27.8% in Q3 2025. Intel remained the dominant supplier with a 64.5% share, down 1% sequentially and 7.7% year-over-year. (Image credit: Mercury Research)Interestingly, Intel managed to slow AMD's advance in the core data center CPU market by apparently substantially increasing shipments of its Xeon SP processors, McCarron believes. When the comparison is limited to AMD's EPYC and Intel's Xeon SP processors, AMD's unit share reached 46.8%, up just 0.4% sequentially, which represents AMD's smallest sequential gain over the past year, as the company's quarterly share gains by this metric averaged 3% over the preceding three quarters.Unlike the client CPU market, the outlook for the server processor market remains particularly favorable for both AMD and Intel. The ongoing buildout of AI infrastructure drives demand not only for conventional data center-grade processors, but also for workstation-class CPUs used in smaller departmental AI servers.SummaryShipments of x86 CPUs declined both sequentially and year-over-year in Q3 2026 to 68.93 million units as rising component prices weighed on client PC demand, while server CPU shipments grew more than 20% year-over-year.Intel regained overall x86 CPU market share from AMD for the first time since Q2 2025, largely thanks to a spectacular comeback in the desktop CPU segment, where its share reached 70.1%. Meanwhile, AMD gained 0.3% of the mobile CPU market, now commanding 29.2%, its highest share ever. Furthermore, AMD reached a record unit share in the server CPU segment, where it now commands 35.5%.Both companies expect client CPU shipments to drop by more than 20% sequentially in Q4, whereas demand for server processors continues to grow due to the ongoing buildout of AI infrastructure. history.titleZh: 英特尔自2025年以来首次夺回CPU整体市场份额
history.descriptionZh:
根据Mercury Research和Jon Peddie Research最新报告，2026年第三季度全球x86 CPU出货量为6893万颗，环比和同比均出现下滑，主要原因是组件价格高企、尤其是内存价格上升，导致客户端PC需求明显走弱；与之形成鲜明对比的是，服务器CPU出货量同比增长约20%，成为近五年来增长最强劲的细分市场。报告统计的是CPU出货量，而CPU通常要数月后才随整机售出，因此这一数据反映的是产业链提前备货和需求预期的变化，而非终端零售销量的即时变化。

从整体市场格局看，Intel自2025年第二季度以来首次从AMD手中夺回整体x86 CPU市场份额。2026年第三季度，AMD整体x86份额为30.10%，Intel为69.90%；AMD环比下降0.7个百分点，但同比仍增长4.5个百分点。若剔除IoT、半定制SoC和嵌入式产品，AMD整体x86份额环比下降0.6%，为多年来首次环比下滑，但同比仍增长4.5%。Intel本季度整体份额回升，主要来自桌面PC CPU出货的意外强劲表现；AMD则在移动和服务器CPU领域继续创下纪录。

客户端CPU市场明显承压。第三季度AMD和Intel合计出货约6080万颗客户端CPU，低于上一季度的6293万颗和2025年同期的约6500万颗。移动处理器需求下降是环比下滑的主因，笔记本CPU出货环比降幅超过10%；桌面CPU出货则有所恢复，主要由Intel带动；服务器和嵌入式CPU继续强劲增长。同比来看，除服务器外，桌面、笔记本、嵌入式和半定制SoC出货均下降。桌面和笔记本CPU下滑源于PC需求疲软及组件成本上升，尤其是内存价格；嵌入式和半定制SoC下降则主要因为AMD游戏主机业务收缩。

在客户端CPU细分市场，AMD份额降至29.3%，低于2026年第二季度创纪录的30.3%，但仍高于2025年同期的25.4%；Intel份额升至70.7%，但明显低于2025年同期的74.6%。Intel的环比份额提升完全来自桌面CPU出货大幅增加，AMD则在笔记本市场继续取得份额增长，只是速度较此前几个季度明显放缓。Mercury Research认为，移动CPU需求疲弱可能使Intel将更多晶圆产能分配给桌面处理器，而这一市场此前较长时间存在供应不足。

桌面CPU成为本季度最引人关注的变化。Intel桌面CPU份额升至70.1%，环比提高5个百分点，同比提高3.7个百分点，实现明显反弹；AMD桌面份额降至29.9%，低于2026年第二季度的34.9%和2025年同期的33.6%，过去一年的份额增益被基本抹去。桌面也是AMD唯一一个环比和同比均失去份额的主要x86 CPU细分市场。报告认为，笔记本处理器需求偏弱使Intel得以向主流桌面CPU分配更多硅片；同时，AMD对游戏PC市场暴露度更高，而游戏显卡供应有限、内存模组和SSD等组件成本异常高，也对其桌面业务造成拖累。

移动CPU方面，第三季度市场环比收缩超过10%，AMD和Intel出货均大幅下降，但AMD降幅略小于Intel，使其移动CPU份额升至创纪录的29.2%，高于2026年第二季度的28.9%和2025年同期的21.9%；Intel仍以70.8%的份额占据主导，但低于上一季度的71.1%和2025年同期的78.1%。AMD环比仅提升0.2个百分点，增幅有限，但同比提升7.2个百分点，在Intel传统强势的笔记本市场表现突出。Mercury Research认为，移动CPU出货环比大幅下降，部分原因是PC厂商将采购提前到了异常强劲的第二季度。展望第四季度，内存及其他组件涨价将推高笔记本价格并抑制终端需求，AMD和Intel均预计客户端CPU出货环比下降超过20%。

服务器CPU市场则延续高景气。2026年第三季度数据中心处理器出货量达到813万颗，同比增长超过20%，为近五年最高年增速，主要受AI基础设施持续建设推动。AMD服务器CPU份额达到创纪录的35.5%，高于2026年第二季度的34.5%和2025年同期的27.8%；Intel份额为64.5%，环比下降1个百分点，同比下降7.7个百分点。Mercury Research分析师认为，Intel通过大幅增加Xeon SP处理器出货，似乎减缓了AMD在核心数据中心CPU市场的推进。若仅比较AMD EPYC与Intel Xeon SP，AMD份额为46.8%，环比仅提升0.4个百分点，为其过去一年最小季度环比增幅，此前三个季度该指标平均每季提升约3个百分点。

整体来看，x86 CPU市场正呈现明显的结构性分化：受内存等组件涨价和PC需求转弱影响，客户端CPU出货下滑，且两家公司均预计第四季度环比降幅超过20%，PC市场困难局面可能延续至2027年上半年；服务器CPU则受益于AI数据中心建设，不仅传统数据中心级处理器需求旺盛，用于小型部门级AI服务器的工作站级CPU也获得拉动。竞争格局上，Intel凭借桌面CPU强劲反弹夺回整体份额，AMD则在移动和服务器市场继续扩大同比优势并创下份额纪录。
